items.title: 68252_Jay Cee
items.q: He's the kind of friend you don't have to see everyday to know they really care.

ctx.x: I once asked him why he identified so strongly with the blacks at a time when things were so rough and he might have been able to pass. And he said, "I figured if I could make it, I could pull a few more along the way." On one of the tapes we have that Fats and J. C. met when Fats was 19, Fats was his dearest, best friend, reminiscing about Fats he

said, quote, "He could get music to talk to him. When he started getting good he'd say, 'talk to me, talk to me, baby.'" Speaking about friends brought a rush of memories. He mentioned Pegleg Bates, who also lives up in our area. And he said this about Pegleg,"several years back Pegleg heard that I might be in financial trouble. That's all he heard. But he sent word down, 'I've got you covered.' He's the kind of friend you don't have to see everyday to know they really care. They did not have to know what the…
Commenting on jazz today he said, "Well, jazz today, the endings get to be dragged out. I'm from the old-fashioned school of music and music should end when it's supposed to."
